title: Tracking the Arc of Vision Loss

patient.name: Mr Ng Boon Huat
patient.presenting_complaint: Follow-up visit — known primary open-angle glaucoma, due for repeat Humphrey Visual Field

history.hpc: Mr Ng has been diagnosed with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) in both eyes for the past 5 years and is on topical IOP-lowering therapy. His IOP has been reasonably controlled (16-18 mmHg) on current medications. He is due for his routine 6-monthly HVF 24-2 SITA Standard to monitor for progression of his visual field defects. He reports no new symptoms but mentions he sometimes bumps into the door frame on his left side.
history.pmhx: POAG both eyes, diagnosed 5 years ago. Hypertension. No previous eye surgery.
history.family_hx: Father had glaucoma and was registered blind in one eye
medications: Latanoprost 0.005% eye drops both eyes nocte
Brinzolamide 1% eye drops both eyes BD
history.social_hx: Retired. Lives with wife. Compliant with eye drops, uses a phone reminder.

examination_findings.fundus: C:D ratio 0.7 right, 0.75 left (per prior doctor's notes) — increased from 0.65/0.7 a year ago

hvf_right.reliability: Fixation losses 1/15 (7%), False positive 3%, False negative 5%
hvf_right.result: Superior arcuate scotoma, denser than previous visit — consistent with progression

hvf_left.reliability: Fixation losses 0/15, False positive 2%, False negative 6%
hvf_left.result: Superior and inferior arcuate scotomas with partial ring scotoma, denser than previous visit — consistent with progression, correlates with patient's reported difficulty on left side

previous_hvf_comparison.trend: Both eyes show worsening mean deviation compared to 6 months ago, left eye more affected

diagnosis: HVF 24-2 SITA Standard performed on both eyes, both tests reliable. Findings show arcuate scotomas in both eyes, denser than the previous visit, with worsening mean deviation — consistent with glaucomatous progression, more marked in the left eye. For doctor's review and consideration of treatment escalation.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and confirm both eyes are to be tested with the 24-2 SITA Standard programme as per his routine monitoring schedule
Ask if patient has done HVF before (he has — less learning effect expected, but still explain briefly)
Check if patient wears glasses for near/intermediate distance and insert the correct trial lens (age-appropriate near correction) into the perimeter's trial frame
Position patient comfortably with chin on chinrest and forehead on forehead rest, patch the eye not being tested
Demonstrate the test: press the button when a light is seen, maintain steady fixation on the central target, do not anticipate
Run the test for the right eye, monitoring for fixation losses, excessive false positives/negatives, and patient fatigue, allowing a short break between eyes if needed
Print reports for both eyes and check reliability indices are within acceptable limits before ending the session
Pull up the previous HVF report for comparison and attach both to the patient's file
Hand reports and the comparison to the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to review HVF results and trend of mean deviation/VFI alongside IOP and disc findings (increased C:D ratio noted)
If progression confirmed despite IOP in target range, doctor may consider escalating treatment (additional medication, laser, or surgery)
Repeat HVF in 6 months or sooner if treatment is escalated, to assess response
patient_education: Explain that this test maps his side vision and helps track how his glaucoma is doing over time
Acknowledge his observation about bumping into the door frame and reassure him this information is helpful for the doctor
Remind him to continue his eye drops as prescribed, as consistent use helps slow progression
Advise him that test results will be discussed with the doctor, who may adjust his treatment plan

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms test programme (24-2 SITA Standard) for both eyes as per monitoring schedule
Elicits the patient's functional symptom (bumping into door frame on left side) as relevant clinical context
Checks for and inserts the correct near/intermediate trial lens correction appropriate to the patient's age and refraction
Reviews medication compliance, which is relevant to interpreting any progression
Sets up the HVF machine correctly with the ordered programme and accurate patient data
Positions patient correctly, patches the untested eye, and gives a clear demonstration of the test
Monitors reliability indices during testing and ensures both tests are reliable before concluding
Retrieves the previous HVF report for direct comparison and attaches it alongside the new results
Recognises the pattern of arcuate scotoma as classic for glaucomatous field loss
Identifies that worsening mean deviation/VFI compared to the prior visit indicates possible progression
Correlates the patient's reported functional symptom (bumping on the left) with the more advanced left eye field loss
Does not make treatment decisions independently — flags progression to doctor for review
Documents HVF results, reliability indices, and trend comparison clearly for both eyes
Hands reports and comparison promptly to doctor given the suspicion of progression
Reinforces medication compliance with the patient
Communicates results in a way that is informative without causing undue alarm
